operations.evidence: Releases in October to December 2025 were 7% lower than in the same quarter of 2024.
The national comparison cannot be mapped to a parcel.
There were 2,624 HDC releases in the latest quarter, 23% fewer than in the same quarter of 2024.
The change is influenced by policy timing and not suitable for location scoring.
There were 105,920 ROTL incidences in the quarter ending December 2025, 25% more than a year earlier; 67% were work-related.
ROTL purpose and volume are operational measures without exact-address relevance.
There were 4,179 people with at least one ROTL incidence and 252 temporary-release failures; more than 99.5% of incidences did not result in failure.
Incidences and individuals use different denominators and must not be converted into a parcel risk rate.
There were 281,688 adjudication outcomes in 2025 and 62% were proven.
Prison adjudications concern conduct in custody and cannot represent community parcel safety.
Proven adjudications increased by 7% to 173,580 in 2025.
The institutional trend has no direct relationship to an address outside custody.
Proven unauthorised-transaction adjudications increased by 8% to 56,129 and disobedience or disrespect adjudications increased by 5% to 51,439.
Custodial disciplinary categories are not community crime categories.
Additional days were awarded on 6,781 occasions in 2025, with an average of 16 days when awarded.
Punishment occasions and average days are custody measures and not spatial risk indicators.
There were 70,275 adjudication outcomes in October to December 2025; 62% were proven and additional days were awarded on 1,838 occasions.
Quarterly adjudications are institutional outcomes without parcel geography.
Proven adjudications rose by 3% to 43,749 and punishments rose by 5% to 133,015 compared with the same quarter in 2024.
Multiple punishments can arise from proven adjudications, so counts must not be conflated or used for parcel scoring.
There were 14,349 licence recalls in October to December 2025, including 573 HDC recalls, 38% more than a year earlier.
Recall totals reflect supervision and policy and are not local incident counts.
There were 6,320 ORA recalls, up 27% year on year, and 8,029 recalls from sentences of 12 months or more, up 48%.
Sentence-group recall statistics cannot identify a local threat.
Latest-quarter recalls were about 38% 14-day fixed-term, 35% 28-day fixed-term, 25% standard determinate, and 1% standard indeterminate recalls.
The distribution is not comparable with periods before July 2025 because recording categories changed.
There were 248,568 offenders under probation supervision at 31 December 2025, 3% more than at 31 December 2024.
A national supervision caseload cannot be attributed to any property or neighbourhood.
